30. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and order of conviction and sentence, the respondent No.1 preferred the Criminal Appeal No. 4393 of 2007 before the High Court Division in which this review petitioner was added as the respondent No.2. Before the High Court Division the appellant-respondent No.1 took 23 grounds in the Memo of Appeal out of which the 1st and the 17th are on law and the rest are on facts. In the 1st ground the respondent No.1 challenged the issuance of notice/order by the Secretary, ACC (Commission in short) under sections 26 and 18 of the ACC Act, 2004 read with Rule 15 gha (I) and (2) of the EPR, 2007 without satisfaction of the Commission ordering to submit statement of assets and liabilities followed by inadequate and untenable investigation and the entire proceedings and trial before the trial Court was initiated illegally and, as such" the impugned judgment and order dated 16-7-2007 is liable to be set aside. In ground No. 17 the respondent No.1 alleged illegality in the judgment and order of the trial court by shifting the burden of proof on the defence instead of usual onus on the part of the prosecution to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt and, as such" the entire findings of the trial Court convicting the respondent No.1 is vitiated by illegality. In the rest of the grounds the respondent No.1 raised illegality on facts of valuation of different assets and liabilities and concealment of information and possession of 6 FDRs worth Taka 1.17 crore which was not disclosed in the statement of assets and the Income Tax Returns and no legal source shown. During hearing 'the respondent No.1 raised new points on sanction asserting that three sanctions are required to be given by the Commission mandatorily. 

 48. The respondent No. 1 of the criminal review petition as the appellant preferred the Criminal Appeal No. 4393 of 2007 before the High Court Division against the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence in which this review petitioner was added as the respondent No.2. In Criminal Appeal No. 4393 of 2007 as many as 23 grounds were taken out of which the 1 st and the 17th are on points of law and the rest are on facts. The 1st ground was in respect of the issuance of notice/order by the Secretary, ACC (Commission in short) under sections 26 and 18 of the ACC Act, 2004 read with Rule 15 gha (1) and (2) of the EPR, 2007 without satisfaction of the Commission followed by inadequate and untenable investigation and the entire proceedings and trial before the trial Court was initiated illegally. The ground No.17 was in respect of illegality in the judgment and order by shifting the burden of proof on the defence instead of usual onus on the part of the prosecution to prove the case beyond reasonable doubt. The rest of the grounds were in respect of illegality on facts of valuation of different assets and liabilities and concealment of information and possession of 6 FDRs worth Tk. 1.17 crore. During hearing of the appeal new points were raised on sanction asserting that three sanctions are required to be given by the Commission mandatorily.
